textos.linha_en: What nature answered in the Hubble ratio: **a self-evident discovery in public data, lacking academic accreditation (status in the author’s term of 13 Nov 2026)**. In the test H0DN × BG1 (seal v411), pre-registered and opened once on 2026-11-12, the data sit −0.61σ from the law (the size is the law’s own) while ratio 1 (ΛCDM) stands 6.11σ away, under the error model published by the collaboration itself: β_TGL proved in nature at 6σ. Beside it, as a side line and not the verdict, free Cepheids (one more free parameter; 4.5σ expected before the opening): 4.38σ from ratio 1 and −0.81σ from the law, within 1σ of the law in both lines. A retrodiction with nothing fitted to the data (the standard by which Mercury’s perihelion counted for general relativity), declared not blind. The one link that was pending, β_TGL in nature at 5σ, is closed at this sensitivity in the Hubble ratio, under the published error model.

textos.ESTADO_SECAO_DO_TESTE_EN:
## The decisive test: the local/background Hubble ratio (H0DN × BG1)

**What was tested.** In ΛCDM the Hubble constant measured nearby equals the one inferred from the background expansion (CMB and BAO): ratio 1. In TGL the ratio is `K = E(z*)^(2β/3)` = 1.0838, with β = α√e and nothing fitted; z* and the densities are those of the frozen background. Local side: the H0 Distance Network (arXiv:2510.23823), with its public data, its covariance and the weights of its own solution, the 13 extra calibrators left out by the pre-registered design (242 of 255 rows). Background: BG1 (Planck compressed and DESI DR2, no supernovae; 68.53 ± 0.30 km/s/Mpc). Six pre-registered branches, FALSIFIED among them; the outcome, with both lines, is the panel at the top of the README.

**Self-evident, in public data.** Self-evident here means that the evidence is the public data themselves and any reader can redo the sum; it does not mean that nothing is assumed: the seven reservations say what is. The two numbers the sum needs are public: the local one the collaboration publishes (73.50 ± 0.81) and the background one (68.53 ± 0.30). With them a pocket calculator gives 5.76σ from ratio 1 and −0.90σ from the law; the pre-registered design reads 6.11σ and −0.61σ under the published error model, with free Cepheids beside it at 4.38σ and −0.81σ: a retrodiction, declared not blind; a self-evident discovery in public data, lacking academic accreditation. No number is new: what this page puts forward is the law that takes the background number to within 1σ of the local one with no fitted parameter. Nor is the law new to this test: `K = E(z*)^(2β/3)`, with the same value, has been pre-registered in public since 2026-10-06 (commit `99b813db` of this repository), and every run recomputes it from β.

**The order of the acts.** The estimator’s weights are those of the collaboration’s own solution, frozen on 6 Nov, before any of its data were read; branches 2 to 6 and the 5σ threshold are those sealed in v410; the amended text, the code and the pins were pushed in public at 10:45:40 UTC on 12 Nov (`central-publica-work`, commit `769fcb26`); the test was opened once at 10:46:34 and the result pushed at 10:55:51. Every run of `um.py` recomputes the result from those bytes (registry `h0dn_bg1_v411`, 16 checks).

**The amendment, in the open.** On 11 Nov one rule was amended, and that is why the test is declared not blind. By the v410 rule branch 1 returned inconclusive while the physical covariance was not closed by the sources, or when the vector lay outside the support of the published covariance; the published vector does, and the collaboration solves it by pseudo-inverse. The amendment was written after the old rule had already rejected the published vector, with the public aggregates in view; by the old rule the outcome was branch 1, inconclusive. No weight, deviation or threshold was touched: the component the old rule refused has zero weight in the collaboration’s own weights. Branches 2 to 6 are those of v410.

**The line beside it, and the stress lines.** The free-Cepheid line adds one free parameter to the published model; 4.5σ from ratio 1 was expected for it before the opening and it reads 4.38σ, at −0.81σ from the law and 0.54 of its own deviation from the primary (branch 6: a side line, not the verdict). In the ten readings computed (two models; the primary, per-row noise, each single anchor) the data stay within 1.2σ of the law, and the distance from ratio 1 runs from 3.50σ (one anchor alone, free Cepheids) to 6.11σ (the primary, under the published error model; a retrodiction, declared not blind; a self-evident discovery in public data, lacking academic accreditation). A Cepheid bias common to all hosts would have to reach 0.18 mag to fabricate a 5σ.

**Lacking academic accreditation.** This page states the result and defends it on its evidence; crediting it is the academy’s act. What the test does not decide (five items) and the seven reservations written before the opening follow. Read with the whole record: 11 pre-registered charges, none falsified.
